text:
Riya Kapoor: Quick heads-up 1: I'm exploring alternative chart stroke treatment for dark mode. On the laptop the thin lines vanish when there are gridlines.
Jonas Lee: Can you attach a screenshot? are we losing contrast or it's an optical blend?
Riya Kapoor: Attached mock (uploaded to the figma comment). The coral series looks fine in the legend but the 1px line reads almost black on the panel.
Kai Nguyen: Might be an ordering issue (grid over lines) or gamma differences. Also check if antialiasing on retina scales down alpha.
Riya Kapoor: Grid is underneath but still. I think it's the hue + size. Two proposals: 1) subtle halo (1px) around lines or 2) slightly boost lightness for strokes <2px.
Ari (a11y): For non-text SVG graphics, WCAG guidance suggests 3:1 contrast for UI components when used to convey information. Tiny strokes count as low-visibility. Halos help. Also consider differentiating dash patterns for multi-series.
Jonas Lee: I prefer the halo for small sizes, it's less noisy than bumping saturation which makes the chart shout. We should only apply halo for stroke widths <=1.5px.
Kai Nguyen: Implementation note: SVG filters can be expensive for many lines. Maybe precompute a second 'glow' path with slightly larger stroke and lower alpha, rendered beneath the main path (cheap).
Riya Kapoor: Good call. I'll add a design token for that: `--chart-stroke-halo: rgba(0,0,0,0.24)` for dark; inverse for light.
Riya Kapoor: Also thinking about syntax/code block on dark: currently monokai-ish accent clashes with UI accents. Proposal: code-bg: #0b1320, code-text: #d6e7ef, code-keyword: #9ad0ff (cooler), strings: #ffd38a (muted).
Ari (a11y): For code blocks, ensure at least 4.5:1 contrast for primary tokens with background if they're semantically important (e.g., errors). For decorative tokens lower is OK.
Jonas Lee: Another nit: chart legend swatches are too saturated relative to surface. Should we use the saturated color for the swatch but a muted label text? or reduce saturation in the swatch itself?
Riya Kapoor: I'd rather keep swatches vivid for quick glances but make the swatch border 1px with `--surface-700` to anchor them. That helps perceived contrast.
DesignBot: FYI: token-change submitted by @Riya — run visual-diff to catch cascading regressions.
Kai Nguyen: UX copy tiny tweak: theme selector label currently "Dark (recommended)". Suggest "Dark 1: higher contrast" to avoid implying recommendation is just preference.
Riya Kapoor: +1 on copy. Also adding a short tooltip explaining why 'higher contrast' matters for dashboards. Links to a11y doc.
Ari (a11y): I'll validate the updated palette with Daltonize and Grabcut tests. Also request a dashboard with min-size sparklines and 2x device pixel ratio to simulate retina.
Jonas Lee: Plan: Riya will push token PR with `--chart-halo` and small stroke variants, Kai will add cheap double-path rendering, Ari runs a11y sim, I'll update legend styles in Figma.
Riya Kapoor: I'll target a PR by 1803459000 with screenshots of before/after and the halo on/off. Thanks team :sparkles:
